residuals: Started blocking native work is not individually aborted by RPC cancellation; existing per-lease budget remains. Result after response abandonment may be committed or unknown.
Generated Go handler decodes protobuf before security interceptor; candidate intentionally authenticates metadata first, so malformed-body/auth error precedence is not qualified.
Native runtime before/after hooks are absent.

Only five signatures are represented, without shrinking the 85-method denominator. No grpc-gateway generated annotations, TLS, reflection, HTTP2 attack/load, SDK, multi-node, HA or production qualification.

Generic Repository interface does not itself certify finite I/O; production PooledRepository retains configured existing pool timeout/cancellation semantics. Cancellation dispatch race remains upstream native residual.
Native gRPC database/oracle evidence must use actual admitted native engines for PostgreSQL and CockroachDB; HTTP auth15 cannot be credited.
Resource caps are local limits, not a claim of Nakama limit equivalence.

Transport force-close is bounded independently of stalled response flushing; total process exit still joins started blocking native work under the existing native pool deadline/cancellation semantics. This does not prove an absolute native I/O termination bound.

Every accepted TCP connection has a local fixed 30-second absolute lifetime, including active healthy clients, not merely idle or pre-request clients. Forced closure can interrupt long-lived sessions or in-flight auth and requires client reconnection; it does not prove no durable effect, grant native per-RPC abort, or permit server-side replay. This is an explicit Nakama lifetime-policy difference.

Lifetime maintenance uses the dedicated runtime supervisor and a 10ms polling interval. The connection admission slot remains occupied after socket shutdown until actual OwnedSocket cleanup; no early reuse is allowed for detached tasks.
